Updated assessment incorporating the Financial Stability Report (FSR):
- The FOMC held the policy rate at 5.25–5.50% and slowed Treasury runoff, citing stalled disinflation despite solid growth and strong employment.
- FSR insights tilt the balance toward caution: elevated interest rate volatility and term-premium sensitivity complicate the outlook; structural vulnerabilities persist in money market funds; leveraged hedge fund activity in Treasury futures/basis trades could amplify stress; commercial real estate—especially offices—faces higher vacancy and refinancing risks that could pressure credit quality; and concerns about public debt and geopolitical tensions add tail risks.
- These stability considerations help justify tapering QT to avoid unnecessary strain on Treasury market functioning while keeping policy restrictive until there is greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably to 2%.
- Net tone: mildly hawkish on inflation but more cautious overall given financial stability vulnerabilities flagged in the FSR—moving the stance from slightly positive to near-neutral.
